History:
- Chief complaint: New-onset headache.
- Onset/duration: Began yesterday mid-morning.
- Location/character: Left-sided, posterior (back of head); throbbing pain that built up over a short period.
- Severity/progression: Reported intensity 8/10; persistent since onset, not clearly worse at any particular time of day.
- Associated symptoms: Denies nausea, vomiting, visual disturbances, photopsia, eye pain, tingling, numbness, weakness, fever, rash, neck stiffness. Ate and drank normally; slept through the night.
- Triggers/relieving factors: No clear triggers identified; ibuprofen (Nurofen) taken yesterday with minimal or no relief.
- Prior episodes: Patient reports headaches are unusual and has not had similar episodes before.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic illnesses: Patient reports no chronic medical problems.
- Family history: Mother with hypertension and history of migraines.
- Allergies: None reported.
- Medications:
  - Ibuprofen (Nurofen) — dose/route/frequency not documented (taken yesterday).
  - Prescribed stronger analgesic recommended by clinician — name/dose/route/frequency not documented (prescription to be collected from pharmacy).
  - Paracetamol recommended as adjunct — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Social history: Lives with partner; occupation: designer. Non-smoker, no alcohol use reported, no recreational drug use.

Physical Examination:
- No formal physical examination findings documented.
- Patient-reported/observed findings:
  - Localized left posterior throbbing headache, 8/10.
  - No focal neurological symptoms reported (no weakness, numbness, or speech disturbance).
  - No visual disturbance, no photophobia, no eye pain.
  - No fever, no rash, no vomiting, no neck stiffness.
- Alertness/orientation: Patient able to provide history during consultation (no explicit exam documented).

Impression:
- Acute left-sided posterior throbbing headache (new onset), moderate-severe (8/10); no associated neurological or systemic features reported on history.

Management Plan:
- Immediate treatment advised:
  - Patient to obtain the clinician-prescribed stronger analgesic from the pharmacy (medication name/dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Take the prescribed analgesic regularly with food.
  - Paracetamol may be taken in addition to the prescribed analgesic (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Continue rest and maintain good hydration.
- Safety netting / indications to seek further care:
  - Return/seek medical attention if pain worsens or does not settle within 1–2 days after trying prescribed treatment.
  - Seek immediate review if new symptoms develop: fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness, or new neurological symptoms.
  - If recurrent episodes of similar headaches occur, further evaluation is required and should be arranged.

Patient Summary:
- 28-year-old female with a new, left posterior throbbing headache started yesterday (8/10) that was minimally responsive to ibuprofen. Clinician has recommended a stronger analgesic (prescription provided) plus paracetamol, rest, and hydration. Patient advised to recontact if symptoms worsen or fail to improve within 1–2 days.

Key Takeaways:
- Take the prescribed stronger analgesic regularly with food; paracetamol may be used concurrently.
- Rest and maintain adequate hydration.
- Return promptly if pain worsens, or if fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness, or new neurological symptoms develop.

Next Steps:
- Patient to collect and begin the prescribed analgesic from the pharmacy.
- Reassess in 24–48 hours if symptoms persist or sooner if new/worsening symptoms occur.
- If recurrent headaches develop, arrange further evaluation and management planning.
